comments: Alternative fit to Saha et al. photometry using 17 high-quality Cepheids on chips 1, 3 and 4. Chip 2 was excluded because its modulus was 0.66 mag larger; including it would give mu0=31.03+/-0.11.

Final ALLFRAME+TRIAL solution. The PL fit uses 27 of 39 candidates with P>20 d to limit incompleteness. All four WFPC2 chips are included because this reduction shows no significant chip-dependent offset.
There are no specific comments on the publication. Cepheid moduli are compiled and homogenized from earlier HST Key Project and independent studies. Previous author included it.

PC-only true modulus from six Cepheids, derived for the differential blending test. It is a chip-specific PL result rather than an adopted global galaxy distance. The quoted uncertainty is internal; no separate systematic term is provided.
WFC-only true modulus from 21 Cepheids. Its offset from the PC result is -0.035+/-0.167 mag, inconsistent with the +0.11 mag shift predicted by severe blending. No metallicity correction was applied.
Uncorrected re-fit of 27 previously selected Cepheids using the Stetson WFPC2 zero point, Udalski OGLE-LMC PL relations and mu_LMC=18.45. Only the internal random R_PL uncertainty is tabulated.

Metallicity-corrected result for the same 27 Cepheids, using gamma_VI=-0.2 mag dex^-1 and the adopted field abundance. The correction raises the modulus by 0.070 mag; the reported internal error is unchanged.

Sandage/Saha HST observations reanalyzed by the Key Project are used. The fit solves simultaneously for distance and reddening. The quoted error is random; the dominant common LMC systematic is omitted.
They use the H band data.
Final period-cut Wesenheit fit before abundance correction. e_R is the random PL-fit error only; N_cef is the post-cut sample.
Table 4 mu_Z, using gamma=-0.2 mag dex^-1 relative to the LMC. Metallicity uncertainty is systematic and excluded from e_R.
Representative LMC mean-light solution. Includes the +0.05 mag STS CTE correction; random error only.
Maximum-light LMC PL solution used as a consistency test. CTE corrected without metallicity correction.
LMC solution with a +0.070 mag metallicity correction. No additional random uncertainty is assigned.
Re-fit of published Gibson et al. (2000) WFPC2 photometry using the OGLE+10 PL relations. The number of retained Cepheids is not stated clearly; the +0.08 mag metallicity correction is not applied.
Adopted distance after a +0.08+/-0.05 mag metallicity correction. The error is statistical from the PL fit and O/H measurement; no per-galaxy systematic or total uncertainty is listed.
STR04 nonlinear, long-period LMC PL solution with metallicity and CTE corrections. Only the random modulus error is reported.
STR04 linear LMC PL solution. The corrected modulus includes the -0.07 mag CTE term. An additional linearity systematic is discussed but not assigned as an individual e_S.
KN04 nonlinear LMC PL solution with period, metallicity, and -0.07 mag CTE corrections. No individual systematic or total modulus error is quoted.
KN04 linear LMC PL solution after the period cut and metallicity and CTE corrections. The table provides random error only.
KN06 linear LMC PL solution, used for the preferred linear H0 calibration. It includes the period cut and metallicity and CTE corrections.
TR02 linear LMC PL solution. It includes a period cut, metallicity correction, and -0.07 mag CTE correction. Random error only is attached to the modulus.
KN06 nonlinear LMC PL solution, preferred for the nonlinear H0 result. The modulus includes period, metallicity, and CTE corrections; its error is random only.
TR02 nonlinear LMC PL solution, including period, metallicity, and CTE corrections. The tabulated uncertainty is random only.
Pure theoretical F160W PL fit for Z=0.02, Y=0.28 and P>10 d. The 49 good Cepheids define the fit; sigma=0.32 mag. Galactic foreground extinction is corrected, with no metallicity term.
